clue.text: Pass round writer taken with European jacket

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: a col is a mountain pass
Kingsley or Martin Amis, the novelists

explanation.surface: Someone hands round a jacket worn by an author travelling with a European.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer sits inside the pass, and the European is tacked on at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole was originally a short sleeved jacket or bodice, before the word came to mean a light undergarment.

clue.text: Girl in plant missing American, an excellent performer?

indicators.note: a word that is missing something has had those letters taken out of it
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

explanation.surface: A young woman hidden in a plant, minus an American: surely a star turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A class act is someone of outstanding quality, here punning on an actual stage performer.

clue.text: Weapon in bag (with cap off) found in Middle East

indicators.note: taking a cap off removes the top, so the word loses its first letter
something found in a place is located inside it, so one piece is housed by another

explanation.surface: A weapon stashed in a bag discovered in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy knife used as a tool and as a weapon.

clue.text: Look around parlour that's been emptied in binge

indicators.note: looking around something surrounds it, so one piece is wrapped about the other
an emptied word has lost its contents, keeping only its outside letters

blocks.note: only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone glances round a drinking parlour left empty after a bender.
explanation.definitionFit: A spree is a bout of unrestrained indulgence, such as drinking or spending.

clue.text: Select deals arranged for Kent tourist attraction

indicators.note: things arranged are put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Special offers arranged for visitors to a Kent attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; the castle is near Maidstone, not in the city of Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds Castle is a moated medieval castle and one of Kent's most visited sights.

clue.text: Tree by seaweed on land

blocks.note: ore is an old word for seaweed, familiar from crosswords

explanation.surface: A tree growing beside washed-up seaweed on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore describes being on the shore or dry ground rather than at sea.

clue.text: Broadcast about an unpleasant Republican in fitting part of London

indicators.note: about in the sense of around, so one word surrounds the following pieces

blocks.note: to sow seed is to scatter it

explanation.surface: News coverage about a nasty Republican in some suitable London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitting' looks like 'suitable' but refers to the fitting of bespoke suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Savile Row in Mayfair is the London street famed for bespoke tailoring, where suits are fitted.

clue.text: Note this is abandoned ground Bond character enters secretly

indicators.note: the two letters of the clue word 'is' are abandoned, i.e. left out of the phrase before it
something ground is crushed and broken up, so the letters are mixed into a new order
a character who enters goes inside, so that letter is placed within the others

blocks.note: the gadget-maker in the James Bond films

explanation.surface: A spy's note on disused land where a Bond figure slips in under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop IS from the first two words, crush what is left, then slip Q in before the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: On the QT is informal for on the quiet, the letters standing for the start and end of quiet.

clue.text: Group of men rag employed put in a stir?

indicators.note: a group of letters taken from the run of words that follow, without changing their order

explanation.surface: Some men hired to make fun of others cause a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' suggests prison, but here it means a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrage someone is to make them furious, putting them in a stir of anger.

clue.text: Hateful low fellows in outstanding debt principally

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so the fellows go within another word
principally means chiefly, first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Scoundrels caught up in large unpaid debts are hateful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding debt' reads as one phrase, but 'outstanding' is the container and 'debt' supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Accursed means detestable or damnable, so it is a strong synonym for hateful.

clue.text: Blockbuster film stolen by chav at arcade

indicators.note: the answer has been taken and is held by the words that follow, tucked inside them

explanation.surface: A youth pinches a DVD of a big film from an amusement arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: A chav is British slang for a brash, loutish youth.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cameron's 2009 picture was one of the highest-grossing films ever made.

clue.text: Noted director from TV seen unexpectedly having prepared talk with composer

indicators.note: something turning up unexpectedly is out of its expected order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a spiel is a glib rehearsed speech

explanation.surface: A famous film-maker unexpectedly appears on television giving a talk alongside a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spielberg is the celebrated Hollywood director of Jaws and E.T.

clue.text: Typical eccentric following favourite

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the eccentric is placed behind the favourite

blocks.note: a character is an odd or quirky person

explanation.surface: A typical oddball comes after the favourite in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' tells us the eccentric comes after the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Behaviour in character is consistent with someone's usual nature, so it is typical of them.

clue.text: Disengaged and cold Shakespearean figure

blocks.note: King Lear, title role of the tragedy

explanation.surface: An aloof, chilly character from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: To be clear of something is to be free of it or detached, as a gear is disengaged.

clue.text: Obscure diet once devised after gourmet's heart

indicators.note: the heart of something is its centre, so only the middle letter is kept
something devised is newly worked out or invented, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: An obscure diet once dreamt up following a food-lover's passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the rearranged letters behind the single letter from the gourmet.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means abstruse, known only to a few specialists.

clue.text: A Conservative minister not deviating from the truth?

blocks.note: a curate is an assistant member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Is a Tory government minister being honest? The question mark hints at doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' suggests a politician, but here it is a minister of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accurate is correct and precise, so it keeps close to the facts.

clue.text: Horse facing stadium with number leaving in unclear situation

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so that letter goes out of the word it was in

blocks.note: a grey is a white or grey horse

explanation.surface: A horse in a stadium with a numbered cloth bolts, causing confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a situation that is ill-defined and falls between clear categories.

clue.text: Western state divided volunteers in Eastern city

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force of volunteers

explanation.surface: Talk of a split US state and volunteers working in an Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcutta, now Kolkata, is the great port city of eastern India.

clue.text: A writer about church beginning to reform is bitter

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

explanation.surface: An author writing about church reform is sharp-tongued.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces simply join, with the pen at the end; 'about' reads only as 'on the subject of', so the clue order of writer and church is not followed.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic means sharp and biting in tone, the same harsh quality as bitter remarks.

clue.text: Composer, first person among royalty, British royalty

blocks.note: the royal we, used by a monarch in place of I

explanation.surface: A composer who was the leading figure among the royals of Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among' looks like a container signal, but the whole phrase defines the royal plural pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Maria von Weber was the German composer of Der Freischütz.

clue.text: Slip in loaf

blocks.note: first meaning: a blunder or mistake
second meaning: a long crusty loaf with diagonal slashes on top

explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a gaffe and also a kind of bread; 'slip' in a loaf suggests baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the embarrassing error and the long rounded white bread share this name.

clue.text: One in field no good when beset by madman

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: a loon is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A cricketer who is useless when harassed by a lunatic.
explanation.walkthrough: Long on is a cricket fielding position deep behind the bowler on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder stationed at long on is one of the players in the field in cricket.

clue.text: Fantastic honeymoon called for poem

indicators.note: fantastic in the sense of fanciful or bizarre, so the letters take on a strange new form

explanation.surface: A wonderful wedding trip calls for some verse.
explanation.walkthrough: A rather gloomy title to come out of such a happy phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats wrote this ode in 1819, one of his great odes alongside the nightingale and the Grecian urn.

clue.text: Egalitarian group with good man in top position

blocks.note: the Commission for Racial Equality, a former UK body

explanation.surface: A group of equals with a decent man in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The CRE was the British Commission for Racial Equality, merged into another body in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: The crest is the summit or highest point of a hill or wave.

clue.text: Trap brought back love for mischievous creature

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the word is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: Someone sets a snare to recapture a lost love, to the delight of a mischief-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Trap and gob are both British slang for mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a small malicious sprite of folklore.

clue.text: Vessel across river showing flag

indicators.note: a vessel lying across a river spans it, so the river sits inside the vessel's letters

explanation.surface: A ship sailing across a river flies its colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant flown from a mast.

clue.text: Element shown in middle of unit?

definitions.text: Element shown in middle of unit?

blocks.clueFragment: Element shown in middle of unit?
blocks.note: surface reading: some component appearing at the centre of a unit
setter's reading: the two central letters of 'unit' are the chemical symbol of a metallic element

explanation.surface: A component sitting at the heart of a single unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Element sounds like a generic part; it is a chemical element whose symbol is Ni.
explanation.definitionFit: Nickel is the metallic element number 28, chemical symbol Ni.

clue.text: Retired Catholic getting unusually irate about Independent standards?

indicators.note: retired in the sense of withdrawn or gone back, so the abbreviation is written backwards
something done unusually departs from its normal form, so the letters are rearranged
about in the sense of around, so the reworked letters surround the next piece

explanation.surface: A retired churchgoer grows strangely angry about falling standards at the Independent newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters wrap around the I for Independent, a nod to the paper this puzzle ran in.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards or tests by which something is judged.
